clue.text: Lancashire town affected by depression on Wearside

parts.note: a col is a dip or pass between two mountain peaks
Wearside, around Sunderland, lies in the North East of England, abbreviated NE

explanation.surface: A northern town hit by an economic slump in the Sunderland area.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Depression' suggests economics or mood, but it is the geographical dip between peaks.
explanation.definitionFit: Colne is a market town in the Pendle district of Lancashire, in north-west England.

clue.text: Leading constituent of the palest variety

indicators.note: a variety is a different version, so the letters of the word are made into another arrangement

explanation.surface: The main ingredient of the lightest kind of something, perhaps an ale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'variety' rearranges PALEST.
explanation.definitionFit: A staple is the main element or chief commodity of something, such as a diet or trade.

clue.text: Exhausted by a kitchen chore

definitions.meaning: having cleaned the plates and pans after a meal

explanation.surface: Someone worn out after doing the dishes.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading is literal: having done the washing-up, a classic kitchen chore.
explanation.definitionFit: Exhausted or finished describes someone spent; done the dishes after a meal is the literal sense of having cleaned plates.

clue.text: Height, say, surrounding an ancient city

indicators.note: surrounding tells us one word goes round the other, enclosing it within

parts.note: to state is to say
Ur was an ancient city of Mesopotamia

explanation.surface: A remark about the tall walls ringing an old city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'surrounding' wraps the state word round the city; 'say' looks like 'for example' but is the verb, and Ur is the Mesopotamian city of Abraham.
explanation.definitionFit: Stature is a person's natural height when standing.

clue.text: Most enduring part of the aircraft?

definitions.text: Most enduring part of the aircraft?

parts.words: Most enduring part of the aircraft?
parts.note: a playful split of a structural aircraft part into a phrase meaning lasting a greater time

explanation.surface: Asking which piece of an aeroplane lasts longest.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer splits as LONGER ON, a jokey reading of 'enduring'; really it is a lengthwise strut of a fuselage.
explanation.definitionFit: A longeron is a main longitudinal structural member in an aircraft's fuselage or wing.

clue.text: Services for all and sundry

definitions.meaning: celebrations of the Eucharist in church

explanation.surface: Church services open to everybody.
explanation.walkthrough: Masses are Catholic church services; the phrase also means the ordinary population.
explanation.definitionFit: Masses are religious services of the Eucharist; the common people at large are everyone, all and sundry.

clue.text: Direction to workers in the Midlands

parts.note: north is a compass direction
worker ants are the crossword's standard workers

explanation.surface: An instruction issued to employees at a Midlands factory.
explanation.walkthrough: Northants is the short name for Northamptonshire, an English county in the East Midlands.
explanation.definitionFit: Northamptonshire, shortened, is a county lying within England's Midlands region.

clue.text: The doctor takes tea and coffee

parts.note: MO is Medical Officer, a doctor
cha is an informal word for tea

explanation.surface: A physician who drinks both tea and coffee.
explanation.walkthrough: CHA (or char) is British slang for tea.
explanation.definitionFit: Mocha is a fine type of coffee, originally shipped from the Yemeni port of that name.

clue.text: Have a concerted bash to raise money

parts.note: to club is to hit, to bash
done jointly, all at once

explanation.surface: Organising a joint party for a fundraiser.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bash' looks like a party but is the verb to strike; the pieces come in answer order though the clue has them reversed.
explanation.definitionFit: To club together is to pool contributions so that a group collects funds for a shared purchase.

clue.text: View of biscuits crisp and spicy

parts.note: ginger snaps are crisp biscuits
hot food is spicy

explanation.surface: An opinion on some crunchy, peppery biscuits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'View' looks like an opinion but is a picture.
explanation.definitionFit: A snapshot is a quick photograph, a captured view of a scene.

clue.text: Vegetable to stick in the shelter

indicators.note: in places the adhesive word inside the word for shelter

parts.note: the lee is the sheltered side, away from the wind
to gum is to stick with glue

explanation.surface: Some vegetable to be stuck inside the garden shed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts the adhesive inside the shelter word; 'stick' looks like a garden cane but is the verb to glue.
explanation.definitionFit: Legumes are podded plants such as peas, beans and lentils, eaten as vegetables.

clue.text: Heavyweight advised to go ahead

definitions.meaning: an instruction to go in front

explanation.surface: A big boxer told to press on.
explanation.walkthrough: The first is the dense metal; the second the imperative 'go first'.
explanation.definitionFit: The metal is famously dense and weighty; telling someone to take the front position urges them to go first.

clue.text: The weed to take the mickey out of an informer

parts.note: to rib is to tease, British 'take the mickey'
a grass is British slang for a police informer

explanation.surface: A weed that mocks a police informant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take the mickey' is British for tease; a 'grass' is someone who informs to the police.
explanation.definitionFit: Ribgrass is ribwort plantain, a common lawn and roadside weed.

clue.text: An amazing sweet store

parts.note: a maze-like structure in which bees keep their sweet product

explanation.surface: Praise for a wonderful confectionery shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'amazing' is read as a-mazing, full of passages like a maze, and the sweet store is the wax cells where bees keep honey.
explanation.definitionFit: Bees build hexagonal wax cells to hold honey, a labyrinthine larder for something sugary.

clue.text: Instruments of power in the armed services

indicators.note: in places the power symbol inside the word for the military

parts.note: the forces are the armed services
P is the physics symbol for power

explanation.surface: The weapons of strength held by the military.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts P inside FORCES.
explanation.definitionFit: Forceps are surgical pincers or tongs, medical tools for gripping.

clue.text: Leap bringing a cry of approval on an Italian island

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means placed after, below the other piece

parts.note: Capri is an island in the Bay of Naples
ole is the Spanish shout of approval

explanation.surface: A jump earning cheers on a holiday island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' in a down clue puts OLE beneath CAPRI.
explanation.definitionFit: A capriole is a leap in dressage, in which the horse jumps and kicks out its hind legs.

clue.text: It can prove difficult to make do and mend on Sunday

indicators.note: on here means the repair word is placed after the day abbreviation, sitting upon it

parts.note: to tinker is to fiddle with repairs

explanation.surface: Doing makeshift repairs on the Sabbath may be hard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make do and mend' was a British wartime slogan for patching things up.
explanation.definitionFit: A stinker is something very hard, such as a tough exam question or puzzle.

clue.text: See 9
A looser form of dispenser

indicators.note: a form of something is a shape it takes, so these letters are moulded into another order

explanation.surface: A less tight kind of dispenser.
explanation.walkthrough: 'form of' rearranges A LOOSER.
explanation.definitionFit: An aerosol is a pressurised can that sprays out its contents as a fine mist.

clue.text: They open out for a novice

indicators.note: out suggests the letters are spread out and put in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Doors are opened for a newcomer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges THEY OPEN.
explanation.definitionFit: A neophyte is a beginner or new convert, someone just starting.

clue.text: Transatlantic jerk?

definitions.meaning: from across the Atlantic, i.e. American

explanation.surface: A tug felt across the ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: From Britain, 'transatlantic' means American; a Yank is an American.
explanation.definitionFit: An American is informally called this by Britons; a sudden pull is the other sense.

clue.text: Transport provided for one-night shows

explanation.surface: Vehicles laid on for a band's single-night concerts.
explanation.walkthrough: Gigs are light two-wheeled horse carriages as well as concerts.
explanation.definitionFit: Light horse-drawn carriages are a mode of travel; musical performances are bookings for bands.

clue.text: Saint on automatic pilot

definitions.meaning: slang name for an aircraft's autopilot

explanation.surface: A holy figure flying on autopilot.
explanation.walkthrough: St George is England's patron saint; 'George' is old RAF slang for an aircraft's autopilot.
explanation.definitionFit: The patron saint of England bears this name, and airmen nicknamed the autopilot by it.

clue.text: Language of many in the end

indicators.note: in places the letter for many inside the word for end

parts.note: a tail is the end of something
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, hence many

explanation.surface: The tongue spoken by many people when all is said and done.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts M inside TAIL.
explanation.definitionFit: Tamil is a Dravidian tongue spoken in southern India and Sri Lanka.

clue.text: Stage order at the opening of a play?

definitions.text: Stage order at the opening of a play?

parts.words: Stage order at the opening of a play?
parts.note: a director's shout to start, also read as the first act being under way

explanation.surface: A director's instruction as the curtain rises.
explanation.walkthrough: The word splits as ACT I ON: the first act is on at a play's opening, and it is the director's call to begin.
explanation.definitionFit: Film and stage directors shout this to start a scene's performance.

clue.text: Too plain to be elective

indicators.note: the letters are to become something else, so they must be rearranged

explanation.surface: Something too dull to be chosen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be' signals that TOO PLAIN becomes another word once rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: An elective course or choice is one that may be taken or left, not compulsory.

clue.text: Perhaps the fish was off

definitions.meaning: an example of a small silvery fish

explanation.surface: Maybe the fish had gone bad.
explanation.walkthrough: The smelt is a small silvery fish; 'smelt' is also the British past tense of smell.
explanation.definitionFit: A small silvery food fish is one sense; to have had a bad odour, gone rotten, is the other.

clue.text: What's that, another invitation?

definitions.meaning: a request to repeat what was said

explanation.surface: Asking a host to repeat themselves, or to invite one back.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase asks someone to repeat what they said, and also invites a guest back.
explanation.definitionFit: A request to repeat what was said, and a request to return for a further visit.
